coordinates: All sampling coordinates are normalized by rotor radius R.
reference: 128-point Gauss-Legendre radial integration with 720 azimuthal points. Each software result is compared with a dense-disk reference using the same aggregation semantics.

methods.sampling: Nine equal-weight points on a square spanning -0.5R to 0.5R in the lateral and vertical directions.
methods.implementation: wcomp/floris_interface.py selects solver type turbine_grid with turbine_grid_points=3. FLORIS TurbineGrid uses average_method=cubic-mean.

methods.sampling: Sixteen cell-center points on a 4 x 4 square spanning the rotor. Weights are the numerically evaluated overlap of each cell with the disk; the four corner cell centers lie just outside the disk but retain partial-cell weight.
methods.implementation: wcomp/foxes_interface.py selects rotor_model=grid16 and partial_wakes=rotor_points. Its CpCtFromTwo turbine uses FOXES REWS, the weighted arithmetic rotor-effective wind speed.

methods.sampling: Four equal-weight points at (+/-R/3, +/-R/3) in the rotor plane.
methods.implementation: wcomp/pywake_interface.py passes GridRotorAvg() to PropagateDownwind. PyWake evaluates wake deficit at each node and takes their arithmetic mean; for uniform ambient inflow this is equivalent to averaging velocity.

cases.name: Uniform inflow
cases.description: A constant field. Any quadrature whose weights sum to one is exact here, so this verifies the harness and the normalization of each stencil rather than discriminating between methods.

cases.name: Linear vertical shear
cases.description: A linear profile. Because all three stencils are symmetric about the hub height, the positive and negative contributions cancel and the area average is still recovered exactly. Point placement starts to matter only once the aggregation is nonlinear.

cases.name: Quadratic radial deficit
cases.description: The first case with real curvature. The exact area average is 0.9. Stencils clustered near the hub under-resolve the slower flow near the blade tips and overpredict the rotor average, which exposes how far each sampling pattern reaches toward the rotor edge.

cases.name: Offset Gaussian velocity deficit
cases.description: A laterally offset deficit that approximates a partially waked rotor. It is neither symmetric nor smooth on the scale of the coarse stencils, so it is the most demanding case and the one most representative of wake-model use.
